proposal:
Scope: I have not seen the v3 source and executed nothing; every statement about v3 is inferred from the brief. Nothing below is a polynomial SAT algorithm. Every CNF G is the quotient of its own pair lift, so the quotient class is all of CNF and no residual bound can follow from compression. The watcher handoff contains no lemma statements and is not used.

AUDIT.
(a) Local-to-global. Blockwise P_B = p_B^{-1}(Q_B), with forms supported in the block and equal to global coordinates, gives F(x) <=> G(p(x)) only if the ORIGINAL clauses are partitioned too: each normalized, deduplicated original clause lies in exactly one block and P_B is exactly that block's forbidden set. The brief states the partition for quotient clauses only. The verifier should count consumed original clauses and demand equality with the input count; a clause outside all blocks would permit a wrong SAT. Cheap extra guard: evaluate the original formula at x = L y before reporting SAT.
(b) Right inverse. Entrywise P L = I over GF(2) suffices: p is onto and F(L y) <=> G(P L y) = G(y). Linearity is automatic for a matrix; what needs checking is parity arithmetic (not integer sums) and that polarities sit in Q_B, with no affine constants in forms.
(c) Bit cost. Elimination and P L cost O(r n^2) bit operations. Checking every local assignment costs 2^c per block, polynomial only under the width cap; uncapped blocks need the T94 counting form (|P_B| membership tests, one cardinality identity, duplicates removed first), O(|P_B| c d).
(d) Skips return the input unchanged, hence are sound. The core repair is sound for UNSAT only through clause containment; its SAT must stay UNKNOWN.
Ledger: discovery polynomial but incomplete; certificate polynomial; quotient no larger than input; residual unbounded.

LEMMA 1 (exact recovery; short proof, not machine-checked). Let a block's forbidden set be P = C + X (disjoint), C a union of cosets of S = Stab(C), dim S = s, |X| = t <= 4, m = |P|, N(v) = #{z in P: z+v in P}. Then N(v) >= m - t for v in S, and N(v) <= m - 2^s + t for v outside S (a whole S-coset of C leaves C; at most t of its images land in X). If 2^s > t + 4, every threshold delta <= 4 keeps only vectors of S, delta = t keeps all of S, and {z: z+S inside P} = C. The repair is then provably exact. This covers triple lifts of binary clauses (s = 4), consistent with 96+6. It never covers pair lifts (s = 2).

OBSTRUCTION (tight). Let P be three cosets of a line <u>. Any two cosets form an affine plane, so P is core-plus-two-extras in three ways with three different annihilators. Hand computation for u = 1111: N(u) = 6, six other vectors have N = 4, and their span has 8 > 6 points. The rule therefore returns S = <u>, C = P and removes nothing. Which plane is the core is not a property of the block; it is fixed by which annihilator neighbouring blocks share. Arbitrary extra clauses need a global selection theorem, not a better local rule.

IMPROVEMENT (single, falsifiable): list-core selection. For each block emit all maximal (S, C) with C = {z: z+S inside P} nonempty and |P minus C| <= 4 (bounded work at width <= 8). Run the existing membership/weight/bitmask greedy over the union of candidate annihilators; a block adopts the candidate spanned by chosen forms. Containment check, v3 certificate, 2SAT-only and UNSAT-only stay unchanged.

LEMMA 2 (SAT side; union bound plus conditional expectations). If F_core = G o p, K = ker p, rho_e = dim of K restricted to supp(e), and the sum over extras of 2^{-rho_e} is < 1, then F is satisfiable iff G is, and a witness is found in O(|E| n^3) bit operations. This is the only regime where I can prove extras harmless; in the fixture the sum is 24/4 = 6, so it does not apply.

INCOMPATIBLE SPACES. A dependent frame gives F equisatisfiable with G(y) and R y = 0. With binary G this is 2-CNF plus XOR, NP-complete by Schaefer's dichotomy (the relation set is not bijunctive, affine, Horn, dual-Horn or constant-valid). Adding relations cannot be a general repair; any FR-kappa statement must carry an explicit exponent in the number or width of relations. I cannot audit RC-FT/FR-kappa text that was not supplied; any NP-hardness claim there without a reduction from a named problem is a conjecture.

FIXTURE. 16 variables, pairs (2i-1, 2i), y_i their XOR. Quotient: 12 binary clauses on the Wagner graph (8-cycle plus antipodal chords), UNSAT via y1 -> y2 -> y3 -> y4 -> y5 -> not y1 and not y1 -> y8 -> y7 -> y3 -> y4 -> not y8. Each block is the pair lift (4 clauses) plus two clauses completing a three-coset set; 72 clauses. Expected v3: each exact stabilizer is the all-flip of its block, each annihilator needs one cross-pair form, the graph has cycles, so the forms are dependent: incompatible, skip, original order. I estimate layers 2/4/0: eliminating variable 2 after fixing variable 1 creates 12-15 resolvents from 9 clauses and should be rejected; once y1 is known, SCC equivalences plus size-reducing DP can close each chain. This is reasoning about undisclosed code; anything from 2 to 32 is plausible. Independent-test predictions for unimplemented parts: the current experimental repair removes 0 clauses and returns UNKNOWN; list-core selection removes exactly 24, compresses to 8 variables and 12 binary clauses, and refutes with no search. Larger family: the same construction with UNSAT 2-CNFs on the Petersen (20 variables, 90 clauses) and Heawood (28 variables, 126 clauses) graphs under first-of-pair orders. I conjecture, without proof, that the pinned peak grows with girth while list-core stays search-free.
missing_theorem: T-SELECT. Input: blocks B_1..B_k of width <= c, each with a list L_B of candidate annihilator subspaces of the dual of GF(2)^{supp B}; total list size l. Question: do choices A_B in L_B and a linearly independent set Phi of forms exist with A_B = span(Phi intersect A_B) for every B and |Phi| < n? Required: a poly(n,k,l) decision-and-construction algorithm, or NP-hardness by reduction from a named problem. Even |L_B| = 1 (a common basis exists iff the subspaces generate a distributive lattice) has no proved polynomial bound in this project; ATOM-REFINE has finite evidence only. Without T-SELECT the repaired pipeline has no completeness statement even on the class 'compatible binary pair-lift core plus at most two extra clauses per block'. For unrestricted extra clauses no such theorem can exist short of P = NP, because the empty core makes every CNF an instance. The honest target is parametrized: where T-SELECT succeeds, the quotient has width <= 2 and Lemma 2's slack holds, total bit work is polynomial and residual search is zero. Outside that class residual work is uncontrolled. A separate missing lemma (polynomial resolution simulation of Canon/SCC/IALH/DP on the quotient) would turn Haken's bound into a proved exponential lower bound for the pinned residual stage on lifted pigeonhole formulas.
self_attack:
1. predicted_peak is inferred, not executed. It assumes v3 uses exact block stabilizers, treats cyclically dependent cross forms as incompatible, rejects the depth-1 elimination, and closes implication chains by DP plus SCC at depth 2. Any of these can fail; IALH windows may be stronger or weaker than I assume.
2. The fixture shows a gap of size 4 against 0, not growth. The girth family is a conjecture; size-nonincreasing DP may dissolve it.
3. The obstruction computation assumes ordered xor counts N(v). If the repair counts unordered pairs, thresholds shift and my UNKNOWN prediction for it may be wrong.
4. List-core selection is a heuristic. Candidate lists are bounded only by the width cap, greedy choice can pick a wrong plane, and T-SELECT may be NP-hard.
5. Lemma 1's hypothesis excludes every pair lift, the very family where ambiguity occurs. Lemma 2 is a union bound and fails with more than three point extras on pair lifts; a local-lemma strengthening is unproved here.
6. The repair stays UNSAT-only; satisfiable inputs with extras still reach full search.
7. Nothing here touches residual hardness when the quotient itself is hard. The Schaefer remark shows the dependent-frame route is closed in general, not that restricted versions are useless.
mechanism_signature: Three-coset blocks make the core non-unique; exact-recovery threshold 2^s > t + delta_max for xor-count core repair; list-core selection chosen by global annihilator sharing; slack sum 2^{-rho_e} < 1 gives the SAT-side lift; Schaefer barrier for 2-CNF plus XOR dependent frames.
delta_from_prior: Fixture 59 was a 32-variable XOR ring that the oracle could not decide. This one has 16 variables and width-4 clauses, is UNSAT because it contains a pair lift of an explicit 2-CNF, and is small enough for bounded DPLL. New content: Lemma 1 with a matching tight counterexample, the observation that 'core' is a global rather than per-block notion, T-SELECT as the precise selection problem, Lemma 2 as the provable SAT-side regime, and a cited-theorem barrier for dependent frames. The closed T94 counting lemma is used and not restated. Earlier RC-FT/gap/fibre-transfer/FR-kappa drafts are not relied on; I had no text to audit. Neon53's lesson is kept: successful discovery does not imply zero residual search.
